Subagent ID: 20261120_43

Fix adversarial-review findings in skills/plugin-script-packaging/ ONLY (Beads task ap-1189.4; no bd/git). Read its AGENTS.md and repo AGENTS.md first. Minimal precise English Markdown edits; SKILL.md <=500 lines.

Findings:
1. MAJOR SKILL.md:69 (also :20 and references/language-typescript.md:5 if similar): "this distribution has no native profile" reads as forbidding native builds for the user's plugin. Reword: "The agent-plugins distribution itself ships no native profile; a user plugin may declare one in its supplied runtime contract." Define "profile" once: "artifact profile = the Git/source or native-archive installation mode declared in the supplied runtime contract".
2. Minor: step 8 (~:74) and step 10 (~:76-78) unconditionally request whole-plugin review via plugin-creator. Make conditional: "For authorized build/verification requests: ..." and "When manifest or layout changed, or the user requested it, recommend whole-plugin source-format review through plugin-creator." Design-only requests return design + proposed checks.
3. Minor: step 7 should say "Before testing or claiming a mode/platform, read the [verification matrix](references/verification-matrix.md)." (local link at the step).
4. Minor: authorized build vs installers: "Build-time locked resolution (e.g. `npm ci`, `cargo build --locked`, `uv export`/locked sync) is part of an authorized build; end-user installers are forbidden only at installation time." Place near steps 4/7/9 consistently.
5. Minor: references/language-python.md:13 proof list: split into "Always:" (lock check, isolated interpreter execution, package-data/Unicode/entrypoint coverage, unsupported-interpreter failures — verify actual items present) and "Only when promised:" (two-build reproducibility; matching-target frozen execution for requested frozen output). Check language-rust/typescript for the same pattern and apply only if equally unconditional.
6. Minor: SKILL.md:75 "Restart the host only if discovery requires session startup" → add "with explicit authority; otherwise report the restart as a pending step."
7. Minor: SKILL.md:94-97 duplicates skill-creator evaluation defaults/override policy; trim to routing to skill-creator plus "never launch models merely to finish packaging" ONLY if tests don't assert the text (tests assert packaging SKILL.md matches /only (?:what the user explicitly requests|when explicitly requested)/, /packaged language runtime\/toolchain is a separate executable closure/, /For Goose Git installation confirm revision/, and must not match /elapsed <seconds>s|first tick after 10 seconds|agent-plugin evaluation|Evaluation defaults:/).
8. Activation description (frontmatter): make it user-vocabulary: e.g. "Designs and verifies contained executable runtimes for Agent Plugin Skills and MCP helpers: vendored npm/uv/Cargo dependencies, launchers, Git-install or native-archive layouts. Use for language-specific dependencies, launchers or explicitly requested cross-platform packaging; not plugin.json review, release publication or wrapped-runtime failure diagnosis." Keep concise third-person.
9. Shared load_skill paragraph (line 46): change final sentence to "If neither call works, read `SKILL.md` directly; report a direct `SKILL.md` read as reading, not activation." keep rest exact.

Also check evals/evals.json and evals/verify-fixture.mjs for anything depending on changed text (do not modify evals unless contradicted). Read tests/test_distribution.test.ts for all plugin-script-packaging assertions. Do not modify tests.

Verify: `node --test tests/test_distribution.test.ts tests/test_goose_hook_compatibility.test.ts`; wc -l SKILL.md. Return changed files, per-finding summary, test results, deferrals.

# Plugin Script Packaging Skill

Follow root instructions; keep this Skill and its references independently copyable.

- Active references govern separately requested external runtimes, not creator/native availability. Retain current normative format sources; remove obsolete workflows rather than treating them as active contracts.
- Do not invent portable dependency fields or vendor schemas. Use a supplied contract or document missing decisions in prose.
- TypeScript, Rust and Python have different runtime closures; Node is not a universal launcher.
- Available skill-creator guidance owns the shared launcher and selected evaluation workflow, exact defaults, invocation, monitoring and output/identity mechanics; no sibling filesystem installation is required. Use defaults unless the user explicitly requests overrides, never inferred from the authoring harness or target host. Creator packaging/install CLIs and native executables remain retired.
- Keep target host, authoring harness, actual installation/proof, evaluation candidate/judge selections and packaged language runtime/toolchain distinct; host-specific rules apply only to their target.
- Route manual whole-plugin review and authorized release to plugin-creator. Evaluation is Skills/Plugins only; history/inspect remain read-only.
- New suites use supported fields only. Declare neutral inputs in `files`; verify execution prerequisites separately and keep independent criteria in the suite, not task prompts. Never launch models or touch live installations to validate authoring.
- `evals/inputs/` contains inert task data and a tiny interpreted JavaScript fixture; `evals/verify-fixture.mjs` tests only disposable copies below this Skill. Neither is a distributed application runtime.
- English metadata/instructions; SKILL.md <=500 lines. No hand-edited generated application runtimes.

## Host version policy

Active instructions target current stable host releases and current official documentation.
Do not teach historical version branches unless the user explicitly requests an older target.
Record agent-plugin version, host/version, feature, evidence and verification status in
compatibility matrices instead. A documented capability is not a tested integration;
unsupported or untested hosts remain explicitly unverified. Refresh upstream before
changing public contracts and keep exact runtime versions in execution provenance.

## Host changes, compatibility matrix and changelog

When a host update (Goose, Claude or another supported agent host) is identified as
changing plugin specifications or behavior, inspect its official changelog/release
notes and the affected documentation or implementation before changing the contract.
Record the host version transition, affected feature/specification, concrete impact
and required adaptation in the compatibility matrix, linked from the corresponding
plugin changelog entry. Include agent-plugin version/source revision, exact host
versions, dated upstream sources, verification evidence and status (documented,
tested, unsupported or unverified). Record no relevant impact only when inspected
evidence supports that conclusion; a version bump alone is not a compatibility result.

Maintain the matrix and plugin changelog together for the authorized change. Preserve
historical rows and prior evidence; do not replace an observed version with a vague
"latest" label. A host changelog claim is documented evidence, not a passed integration
test. Keep ordinary Skill instructions on the current supported behavior rather than
adding historical branches. If no plugin changelog/location exists, report that gap
and confirm its destination before creating one; never invent an entry or imply a
release occurred. Missing verification stays explicit and is tracked in Beads.

This maintenance obligation authorizes neither automatic installation/upgrades nor
credentials, model execution, commits, pushes or publication. Apply current task
scope and action-specific authorization before any such operation.

### Compatibility range per agent-plugin version

For each agent-plugin release, state the declared supported host range separately
from exact observed versions, for example `Goose >=1.40.0` (illustrative only, not
an established minimum). A range is a support commitment; derive its lower bound
from the required capabilities and inspected host evidence, record its rationale,
exceptions/upper bound when applicable, and verify the boundary before labeling
it tested. Do not infer `>=` compatibility from one successful newer version.
Keep exact tested host versions and results in separate evidence columns; identify
untested versions within a declared range explicitly. A later host regression must
update the range/limitations and linked plugin changelog rather than silently
retaining an unlimited `+` claim. Unknown lower bounds remain unverified, not guessed.
